title: Grade 11 Chemistry — Equilibrium
description: Chemical Equilibrium — Le Chatelier's principle, Kc, Kp, ionic equilibrium, pH (CBSE Ch. 7)
subject: chemistry

questions.question: In a reversible reaction at equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the:
questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium: the forward and reverse reactions continue simultaneously at equal rates. The concentrations of reactants and products remain constant (not zero), but the reaction has not stopped.

questions.question: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), the expression for Kc is:
questions.explanation: Kc = [products]^stoich / [reactants]^stoich = [NH₃]² / ([N₂][H₂]³). Always products over reactants, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient.

questions.question: Kp and Kc are related by: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. Here Δn is:
options: Moles of gaseous products − moles of gaseous reactants
questions.explanation: Δn = (moles of gaseous products) − (moles of gaseous reactants). For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: Δn = 2 − (1+3) = −2. Note: only gaseous species are counted; solids and liquids are excluded.

questions.question: Le Chatelier's principle states that if a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it will:
options: Shift to oppose the disturbance and re-establish equilibrium
questions.explanation: Le Chatelier's principle: a system at equilibrium responds to a stress (change in concentration, pressure, or temperature) by shifting in the direction that minimises the effect of the stress.

questions.question: For the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ + heat, increasing temperature will:
questions.explanation: This is an exothermic reaction. Adding heat (increasing T) shifts the equilibrium left (toward reactants, away from NH₃) to absorb the added heat. This also decreases Kc.

questions.question: Adding an inert gas at constant volume to an equilibrium mixture:
options: Shifts the equilibrium to the side with more moles of gas
Shifts the equilibrium to the side with fewer moles of gas
questions.explanation: At constant volume, adding an inert gas increases total pressure but does NOT change the partial pressures of reacting species (their concentrations are unchanged). So the equilibrium is unaffected.

questions.question: A Kc > 1 indicates that at equilibrium:
options: Equal concentrations of reactants and products
The reaction is at a very early stage
questions.explanation: Kc = [products]/[reactants]. Kc > 1 means [products] > [reactants] at equilibrium → products are favoured. Kc ≫ 1 means the reaction goes essentially to completion; Kc ≪ 1 means reactants are favoured.

questions.question: The reaction quotient Q is used to:
options: Calculate the equilibrium constant at a new temperature
Predict the direction in which a reaction will proceed to reach equilibrium
Measure the rate of the forward reaction
questions.explanation: Q has the same form as Kc but uses current (non-equilibrium) concentrations. If Q < Kc → forward reaction proceeds; Q > Kc → reverse reaction proceeds; Q = Kc → system is at equilibrium.

questions.question: Ionic equilibrium: The degree of ionisation of a weak acid increases when:
options: Concentration of the acid is increased
Concentration of the acid is decreased (dilution)
A common ion (like sodium acetate) is added
questions.explanation: On dilution, Le Chatelier's principle predicts a shift toward more ionisation to oppose the decrease in ion concentrations. So α (degree of ionisation) increases with dilution. The common ion effect (option D) suppresses ionisation.

questions.question: The pH of a 0.01 M strong acid HCl solution is:
questions.explanation: HCl is fully dissociated. [H⁺] = 0.01 M = 10⁻². pH = −log[H⁺] = −log(10⁻²) = 2.

questions.question: Ka for acetic acid at 25°C is 1.8 × 10⁻⁵. The pKa is approximately:
A buffer solution resists change in pH when:
options: A strong acid or base is added in large quantities
Small amounts of acid or base are added
questions.explanation: A buffer (weak acid + its conjugate base, or weak base + its conjugate acid) resists pH change when small amounts of acid or base are added, because the added H⁺ or OH⁻ is consumed by the buffer components.

questions.question: The common ion effect: adding sodium acetate (CH₃COONa) to acetic acid solution will:
questions.explanation: Sodium acetate provides CH₃COO⁻ ions. By Le Chatelier's principle, this suppresses the ionisation of CH₃COOH (common ion effect), decreasing [H⁺] and raising the pH.

questions.question: Kw (ionic product of water) at 25°C is:
questions.explanation: Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C. In pure water [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ M, giving pH = 7. Kw increases with temperature (water ionisation is endothermic).

questions.question: Increasing pressure on the Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃) shifts equilibrium to produce more NH₃ because:
options: The forward reaction produces fewer moles of gas (2 vs 4) so it is favoured
Higher pressure increases the rate constant Kc
NH₃ is a gas and is compressed
questions.explanation: Le Chatelier's principle: increased pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas. The forward reaction: 1+3 = 4 moles → 2 moles. So higher pressure shifts equilibrium to the right (toward NH₃). Note: Kc itself is unchanged by pressure.
